candidates.phrase: The Son, who is the Word of the Father, the very and eternal God
candidates.rationale: Directly names the Son as the eternal Word, very and eternal God, asserting the filial identity of the Logos.
candidates.chunk_text: The Son, who is the Word of the Father, the very and eternal God, of one substance with the Father, took man's nature in the womb of the blessed Virgin; so that two whole and perfect natures, that is to say, the Godhead and Manhood, were joined together in one person, never to be divided; whereof is one Christ, very God and very Man, who truly suffered, was crucified, dead, and buried, to reconcile his Father to us, and to be a sacrifice, not only for original guilt, but also for actual sins of men.

candidates.phrase: He is the eternal Word made flesh, the only begotten Son of the Father
candidates.rationale: Directly names the eternal Son as the Logos ('eternal Word'), begotten of the Father, affirming the filial relation.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe in Jesus Christ, truly God and truly man, in whom the divine and human natures are perfectly and inseparably united. He is the eternal Word made flesh, the only begotten Son of the Father, born of the Virgin Mary by the power of the Holy Spirit. As ministering Servant he lived, suffered and died on the cross. He was buried, rose from the dead and ascended into heaven to be with the Father, from whence he shall return. He is eternal Savior and Mediator, who intercedes for us, and by him all men will be judged.

candidates.phrase: Father, Son and Holy Spirit, distinct but inseparable, eternally one in essence and power
candidates.rationale: Confesses the Son as an eternal, distinct yet consubstantial person of the Trinity, affirming his eternal filial identity as divine.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe in the one true, holy and living God, Eternal Spirit, who is Creator, Sovereign and Preserver of all things visible and invisible. He is infinite in power, wisdom, justice, goodness and love, and rules with gracious regard for the well-being and salvation of men, to the glory of his name. We believe the one God reveals himself as the Trinity: Father, Son and Holy Spirit, distinct but inseparable, eternally one in essence and power.

candidates.phrase: who proceeds from and is one in being with the Father and the Son
candidates.rationale: Implicitly affirms the Son shares one being with the Father, supporting his divine eternal status, though the main subject is the Spirit.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe in the Holy Spirit who proceeds from and is one in being with the Father and the Son. He convinces the world of sin, of righteousness and of judgment. He leads men through faithful response to the gospel into the fellowship of the Church. He comforts, sustains and empowers the faithful and guides them into all truth.

candidates.phrase: We believe in Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son of God
candidates.rationale: Directly names the eternal Son as the only begotten Son of God, truly God and truly man, asserting divine filial identity.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe in Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son of God. He was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin Mary, truly God and truly man. He died on the cross and was buried, to be a sacrifice both for original sin and for all human transgressions, and to reconcile us to God. Christ rose bodily from the dead, and ascended into heaven, and there intercedes for us at the Father’s right hand until He returns to judge all humanity at the last day.

candidates.locator: Article 1. Faith in the Holy Trinity, ¶210
candidates.phrase: three persons of one essential nature, power and eternity — the Father, the Son
candidates.rationale: Confesses the Son as one of three co-eternal persons sharing one essential divine nature, affirming eternal filial identity within the Godhead.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe in the one living and true God, both holy and loving, eternal, unlimited in power, wisdom and goodness, the Creator and Preserver of all things. Within this unity there are three persons of one essential nature, power and eternity — the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

candidates.phrase: is of the same essential nature, majesty, and glory, as the Father and the Son
candidates.rationale: Affirms the Son shares the same essential divine nature and glory as the Father, though the sentence's grammatical subject is the Spirit.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe in the Holy Spirit who proceeds from the Father and the Son, and is of the same essential nature, majesty, and glory, as the Father and the Son, truly and eternally God. He is the Administrator of grace to all, and is particularly the effective Agent in conviction for sin, in regeneration, in sanctification, and in glorification. He is ever present, assuring, preserving, guiding, and enabling the believer.
